attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I feel positive about this paper. My overall impression is good, and I'd be pleased to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-2z73k283/call-a3347978c85e4c6e8050b7b27a4f8284/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
text='\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+page.extract_text() for i,page in enumerate(r.pages))
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:25000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for name in ['manuscript.txt','page-10-detail.png']+[f'page-{i:02d}.png' for i in range(1,13)]:
 (p/name).unlink(missing_ok=True)
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary review files; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: The problem has an identifiable audience in program representation learning, software engineering, and reverse engineering. Transferring information from source code and generated summaries into an encoder that subsequently needs only the low-level representation is a useful direction.
The reported results are promising. Function-name accuracy improves from the strongest evaluated baseline’s 29.41% to 33.41%, and summarization BLEU-4 improves from 32.43 to 34.36.

The evaluation covers four downstream tasks and includes ablations of comments, encoder anchoring, and interpolation. The overview figures and Algorithm 1 make the high-level training pipeline understandable.
weaknesses: Necessary: Align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. Sections 3.1–3.2 use compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function, global, and type names. This does not establish performance on representations recovered from stripped executables; the footnote describing these representations as trivially interchangeable is inaccurate. Either evaluate that deployment setting or consistently narrow the claims to the compiler-generated LLVM representation actually studied.

Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Table 2 assigns 64/16/24 non-overlapping problem labels to training/development/test, yet the task is described as supervised classification into 104 classes. Ordinary supervised classification does not explain predictions for unseen classes. If this is retrieval, specify the query/candidate construction, training objective, and metric definitions. Also reconcile the AnghaBench validation-set evaluation in Section 3.2 with the test-set wording in Section 4.3 and explain checkpoint selection.

Necessary: Specify the implemented model and objective sufficiently for reproduction. Equation 4 omits the softmax described immediately above it, leaving unnormalized similarities as cross-entropy targets in Equation 5. Clarify target normalization and gradient handling, encoder architectures and initialization, tokenization, and downstream prediction heads/decoders. Reconcile random selection of two modalities with the statement that only the binary encoder is trainable.

Necessary: Strengthen the attribution of improvements to interpolation. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full models receive 30 or 70. Section 4.5 asserts PCL convergence without presenting supporting evidence, and the experiments do not isolate linear interpolation, feature-wise interpolation, or their ordering. Match training budgets or substantiate convergence, and limit component-specific claims accordingly. Report uncertainty or qualify small differences: Table 6’s exact-match advantage over GraphCodeBERT is only 0.43 percentage points, while its BLEU-4 is lower.

Necessary: Distinguish lexical agreement from semantic correctness and human usefulness. The summaries are generated by CodeT5, and the comprehension evaluation mainly measures overlap with reference text. There is no reported human-perception study despite RQ2, nor compilation or behavioral validation of generated source. Figure 7 also presents GraphCodeBERT’s 'Unloads the mutex' as inferior to the essentially equivalent 'Unloads a mutex.' Add appropriate semantic validation or narrow the conclusions to the measured text-generation outcomes.

Necessary: Correct the embedding analysis in Section 4.1. Unique programs can legitimately form semantic clusters, and fewer clusters in separately fitted t-SNE visualizations do not prove better representations. These plots cannot establish the claimed embedding-quality improvement. Likewise, human gradual learning and preservation of program semantics under interpolation are motivations rather than demonstrated mechanisms; present them as hypotheses or provide direct evidence.

Optional: Comparisons with binary-specific encoders, experiments across compiler optimization settings, and training-cost measurements would improve practical positioning. Consistent dataset names, metric labels, and table references would improve readability. These extensions are secondary to resolving the evidence and reproducibility concerns above.
